question: Why do the cheapest Mars launch windows come round only about every 15 years, not every 26 months?
answer: Because Mars's orbit is lopsided. Its distance from the Sun swings between about 207 and 249 million km, so some windows aim at a nearer Mars than others. Seven windows of about 26 months add up to 15 years, almost exactly eight Martian years, so only then does the same geometry come back.
move: When two cycles nearly share a multiple, expect a slow rhythm on top.
reference: Sergeyevsky, Snyder & Cunniff, Interplanetary Mission Design Handbook, Volume I, Part 2: Earth to Mars Ballistic Mission Opportunities, 1990–2005, JPL Publication 82-43, 1983
